lines.en: In November 2025, Microsoft's CEO said something strange.
lines.zh: 2025 年 11 月，微软的 CEO 说了一句奇怪的话。

lines.en: His company may have a bunch of AI chips sitting in inventory — that it can't plug in.
lines.zh: 他们可能有一大批 AI 芯片躺在库存里，插不上电。

lines.en: The chips weren't the problem. The problem, in his words, was power.
lines.zh: 问题不在芯片。用他的话说，问题在电。

lines.en: So here's the question: will electricity become the ceiling on AI?
lines.zh: 所以问题来了：电，会不会成为 AI 的天花板？

lines.en: My answer is yes. But not in the way you think.
lines.zh: 我的答案是：会。但不是你想的那种方式。

lines.en: Because the thing that's really running out might not be electricity at all.
lines.zh: 因为真正不够用的，可能根本不是电。

lines.en: First, why does AI need so much electricity in the first place?
lines.zh: 先说说，AI 到底为什么这么耗电？

lines.en: Data centers are built from racks, tall cabinets packed with computers.
lines.zh: 数据中心是由一个个机柜组成的，就是塞满电脑的高柜子。

lines.en: In 2024, the average rack drew under 8 kilowatts.
lines.zh: 2024 年，一个机柜平均用电不到 8 千瓦。

lines.en: A single rack of Nvidia's GB200 AI system is estimated to draw around 120.
lines.zh: 而英伟达 GB200 AI 系统的一个机柜，估计要用大约 120 千瓦。

lines.en: That's roughly fifteen times as much, in one cabinet.
lines.zh: 一个柜子，差不多是普通机柜的 15 倍。

lines.en: Now fill a whole campus with them. Elon Musk's xAI already runs about one and a half gigawatts of its own power plants for its data centers in Memphis.
lines.zh: 现在把整个园区都装满这种机柜。马斯克的 xAI，光在孟菲斯就为自己的数据中心配了大约 1.5 吉瓦的自建电站。

lines.en: One gigawatt, running around the clock, is about what 800,000 average American homes use.
lines.zh: 1 吉瓦全天候运转，大约相当于 80 万户美国普通家庭的用电量。

lines.en: Add it all up, and in 2024, data centers worldwide used about 415 terawatt-hours of electricity.
lines.zh: 全部加起来，2024 年全球数据中心用了大约 415 太瓦时的电。

lines.en: That's around one and a half percent of all the electricity the world uses.
lines.zh: 大约占全世界用电量的 1.5%。

lines.en: One and a half percent doesn't sound like a crisis.
lines.zh: 1.5%，听起来不像什么危机。

lines.en: But the International Energy Agency expects it to more than double by 2030, to around 945 terawatt-hours.
lines.zh: 但国际能源署预计，到 2030 年这个数字会翻一倍多，达到约 945 太瓦时。

lines.en: That's slightly more than all of Japan uses today.
lines.zh: 比整个日本今天的用电量还略多一点。

lines.en: And it's concentrated. The United States alone accounts for about 45 percent of data center electricity.
lines.zh: 而且非常集中。光美国一家，就占了全球数据中心用电的约 45%。

lines.en: Through 2030, data centers are expected to drive nearly half of America's growth in electricity demand.
lines.zh: 到 2030 年，美国新增的用电需求里，预计将近一半来自数据中心。

lines.en: You might think: chips keep getting more efficient. Won't that solve it?
lines.zh: 你可能会想：芯片越来越省电，问题不就解决了吗？

lines.en: They are getting more efficient. Nvidia says its newest system delivers up to 25 times more performance at the same power than the previous generation, on certain AI tasks.
lines.zh: 芯片确实越来越省电。英伟达说，在某些 AI 任务上，它最新的系统在同样的用电下，性能最高是上一代的 25 倍。

lines.en: And yet, data center electricity use has grown about 12 percent a year since 2017, more than four times faster than electricity use overall.
lines.zh: 但从 2017 年到现在，数据中心的用电量每年增长约 12%，是全社会用电增速的四倍多。

lines.en: This is an old story. In 1865, the economist William Stanley Jevons noticed that more efficient steam engines didn't cut Britain's coal use. They increased it.
lines.zh: 这是个老故事了。1865 年，经济学家杰文斯发现：更高效的蒸汽机并没有让英国少烧煤，反而让英国烧得更多了。

lines.en: When something gets cheaper to use, we find far more ways to use it.
lines.zh: 一样东西用起来越便宜，我们就会找到越多的用法。

lines.en: Cheaper AI means more AI. Efficiency doesn't shrink the bill. It grows the appetite.
lines.zh: AI 越便宜，用的人就越多。效率不会让账单变小，只会让胃口变大。

lines.en: Here's what most people miss.
lines.zh: 但大多数人没注意到这一点。

lines.en: The world isn't running out of electricity. It's running out of time to connect it.
lines.zh: 世界不是电不够了，而是来不及把电接过来。

lines.en: A data center is just a building. Feeding it takes a whole chain: power plants, transmission lines, transformers.
lines.zh: 数据中心只是一栋楼。给它供电，需要一整条链：发电厂、输电线、变压器。

lines.en: And every link in that chain has a waiting line.
lines.zh: 而这条链上的每一环，都在排队。

lines.en: Start with power plants. In the US, a new power project has to apply to connect to the grid, then wait its turn.
lines.zh: 先说发电厂。在美国，新建一个发电项目，要先申请接入电网，然后排队等着。

lines.en: At the end of 2025, more than 2,000 gigawatts of generation and storage were sitting in those lines.
lines.zh: 到 2025 年底，排在队伍里的发电和储能项目，加起来超过 2000 吉瓦。

lines.en: For projects that finally came online in 2025, the typical wait from application to switching on was more than five years.
lines.zh: 2025 年终于建成的项目，从申请到真正发电，中位等待时间超过 5 年。

lines.en: And most never make it at all. Of everything that applied between 2000 and 2020, only 13 percent was ever built.
lines.zh: 而且大多数项目根本建不成。2000 到 2020 年申请的项目里，最后真正建成的只有 13%。

lines.en: New transmission lines in advanced economies take four to eight years to build.
lines.zh: 在发达经济体，建一条新的输电线要 4 到 8 年。

lines.en: Large power transformers now have lead times of up to four years, and prices have jumped roughly 80 percent in five years.
lines.zh: 大型变压器的交货期已经拉长到最多 4 年，价格五年里涨了大约 80%。

lines.en: Gas turbines? GE Vernova, one of the biggest makers, said in December 2025 that it was sold out through 2028.
lines.zh: 燃气轮机呢？最大的制造商之一 GE Vernova 在 2025 年 12 月说，2028 年以前的产能已经卖光了。

lines.en: The IEA estimates that, unless these bottlenecks are fixed, around 20 percent of planned data center projects could be delayed.
lines.zh: 国际能源署估计，如果这些瓶颈解决不了，大约 20% 的在建数据中心项目可能延期。

lines.en: In September 2026, Morgan Stanley put a number on the gap: a shortfall of about 32 gigawatts for US data centers through 2028.
lines.zh: 2026 年 9 月，摩根士丹利算了一下缺口：到 2028 年，美国数据中心大约缺 32 吉瓦的电。

lines.en: That's roughly a third of what they need.
lines.zh: 差不多是需求的三分之一。

lines.en: Chips move on product cycles. Power moves on permit and construction cycles, and those run five years and more.
lines.zh: 芯片按产品周期更新，电力却要按审批和施工的周期走，而这个周期动不动就是五年以上。

lines.en: When something is scarce, its price tells you.
lines.zh: 一样东西缺不缺，看价格就知道。

lines.en: PJM runs the power grid across all or parts of 13 US states and Washington, D.C.
lines.zh: PJM 负责管理美国 13 个州（全部或部分地区）加上华盛顿特区的电网。

lines.en: Every year, it holds an auction for future power supply.
lines.zh: 它每年都会拍卖未来的供电能力。

lines.en: For 2024 to 2025, the price was about 29 dollars per megawatt-day.
lines.zh: 2024 到 2025 年度，价格大约是每兆瓦每天 29 美元。

lines.en: For 2027 to 2028, it hit 333 dollars, the maximum the rules allowed.
lines.zh: 到了 2027 到 2028 年度，价格涨到 333 美元，碰到了规则允许的上限。

lines.en: Analysts estimate that without the cap, it would have been close to 530.
lines.zh: 分析师估计，如果没有上限，价格会接近 530 美元。

lines.en: And even at that price, the auction still fell short of its reliability target.
lines.zh: 而且就算开出这个价，拍卖还是没凑够保障供电稳定所需的量。

lines.en: The reason? PJM's demand forecast jumped by 5,250 megawatts, almost entirely because of data centers.
lines.zh: 原因呢？PJM 预测的用电需求一下子多了 5250 兆瓦，几乎全是因为数据中心。

lines.en: And that cost doesn't stay with tech companies.
lines.zh: 而这笔钱，不只是科技公司在付。

lines.en: In Washington, D.C., one utility's residential customers saw bills rise about 21 dollars a month starting in June 2025, around 10 of it from these capacity prices.
lines.zh: 在华盛顿特区，一家电力公司的居民用户从 2025 年 6 月起，电费每月涨了约 21 美元，其中约 10 美元来自这类容量价格。

lines.en: So the tech giants stopped waiting.
lines.zh: 于是，科技巨头们不等了。

lines.en: Microsoft signed a deal to bring back a reactor at Three Mile Island, which shut down in 2019. It's now expected back online in 2027.
lines.zh: 微软签了协议，让三哩岛一座 2019 年就关掉的核反应堆重新启动，现在预计 2027 年恢复发电。

lines.en: Google signed up for small nuclear reactors from a company called Kairos Power: up to 500 megawatts, with the first targeted for 2030 and the rest by 2035.
lines.zh: 谷歌向一家叫 Kairos Power 的公司订了小型核反应堆：最多 500 兆瓦，第一座目标 2030 年投运，其余的到 2035 年。

lines.en: Notice the dates. Even the fixes run on the grid's clock, not the chip's.
lines.zh: 注意这些年份。就连解决办法，走的也是电网的时钟，而不是芯片的时钟。

lines.en: Others are skipping the grid entirely.
lines.zh: 还有人干脆绕开电网。

lines.en: One analysis counted 59 US data center projects planning about 90 gigawatts of their own on-site power.
lines.zh: 一份分析统计，美国有 59 个数据中心项目计划自建现场发电，总共约 90 吉瓦。

lines.en: That's more than a quarter of all planned data center capacity in the country.
lines.zh: 这超过了全美规划中数据中心总容量的四分之一。

lines.en: And 92 percent of those projects were announced since the start of 2025.
lines.zh: 而其中 92% 的项目，都是 2025 年以后才宣布的。

lines.en: But here's the catch. As of mid-2026, only about 2 gigawatts of that was actually running. Roughly 2 percent.
lines.zh: 但问题来了：截至 2026 年年中，真正在运行的只有大约 2 吉瓦，差不多只占 2%。

lines.en: Announcing a power plant is easy. Building one is the bottleneck.
lines.zh: 宣布要建电厂很容易，真正建起来才是瓶颈。

lines.en: It got strange. In December 2025, Crusoe, a company that builds AI data centers, ordered 29 gas turbines from Boom Supersonic, a startup best known for designing supersonic jets.
lines.zh: 事情开始变得离奇。2025 年 12 月，AI 数据中心建造商 Crusoe 向 Boom Supersonic 订了 29 台燃气轮机，而这家公司最出名的是设计超音速客机。

lines.en: Then, in September 2026, Crusoe walked away from that deal and turned to established suppliers like GE Vernova.
lines.zh: 结果到了 2026 年 9 月，Crusoe 放弃了这笔订单，转向 GE Vernova 这样的老牌供应商。

lines.en: When time is the bottleneck, an untested machine is a risk few can afford.
lines.zh: 当时间就是瓶颈，没被验证过的机器，是很少有人敢冒的险。

lines.en: Now flip the map.
lines.zh: 现在，把地图翻过来。

lines.en: China generates more than twice as much electricity as the United States.
lines.zh: 中国的发电量，是美国的两倍多。

lines.en: In 2025 alone, it added more than 430 gigawatts of wind and solar capacity.
lines.zh: 光是 2025 年一年，中国就新增了超过 430 吉瓦的风电和光伏装机。

lines.en: BloombergNEF expects China to add more than six times as much generation capacity as the US over the next five years.
lines.zh: 彭博新能源财经预计，未来五年，中国新增的发电装机将是美国的六倍多。

lines.en: One business school researcher put it simply: the US has the chips and is short on power. China has the power and is short on chips.
lines.zh: 一位商学院的研究者说得很直白：美国有芯片、缺电；中国有电、缺芯片。

lines.en: So electricity isn't one ceiling. It's a different ceiling, depending on where you stand.
lines.zh: 所以电不是一块天花板。站在哪里，天花板就不一样。

lines.en: So here's my call.
lines.zh: 所以，我的判断是：

lines.en: Electricity won't stop AI. Too much money is chasing this problem for that.
lines.zh: 电挡不住 AI，追着这个问题砸的钱太多了。

lines.en: But for the next few years, power will decide three things: how fast AI grows, where it gets built, and who wins.
lines.zh: 但未来几年，电会决定三件事：AI 长得多快、建在哪里，以及谁会赢。

lines.en: The winners won't just be the ones with the best models. They'll be the ones who locked in power early.
lines.zh: 赢家不只是模型最好的那家，而是最早锁定电力的那家。

lines.en: I'd go further: by the end of this decade, a guaranteed grid connection may be worth more than the chips you plug into it.
lines.zh: 我甚至觉得：到这个十年结束时，一个有保障的电网接口，可能比插在上面的芯片还值钱。

lines.en: And if I'm wrong, it'll be because the grid suddenly started moving at chip speed: new lines, plants and transformers arriving in two or three years instead of five or more. That's the signal to watch.
lines.zh: 如果我错了，那一定是因为电网突然跑出了芯片的速度：新的输电线、电厂和变压器，两三年就能到位，而不是五年以上。这就是值得盯住的信号。

lines.en: What does this mean for you?
lines.zh: 这和你有什么关系？

lines.en: If you live where data centers are booming, part of AI's bill may already be on your electricity bill.
lines.zh: 如果你住在数据中心扎堆的地方，AI 的一部分账单，可能已经算进你的电费里了。

lines.en: And next time someone says AI is limited by chips, remember Microsoft's problem. The chips were there. The power wasn't.
lines.zh: 下次再有人说 AI 卡在芯片上，想想微软的问题：芯片有了，电没有。

lines.en: So which do you think runs out first: chips, or electricity? Tell me in the comments.
lines.zh: 那你觉得，芯片和电，哪个会先不够用？评论区告诉我。
